newsitem.title: UK: UK mortgage lending shows more balance in Q2 - bank.
newsitem.headline: UK mortgage lending shows more balance in Q2 - bank.

text.p: Britain's mortgage market is now showing a pattern of stability across all parts of the country, said Barclays Plc's Mortgages on Tuesday.
This follows a period of volatility during 1996 which included an extreme surge in activity levels in the south of England, said the mortgage lender in a statement.
Mortgage lending growth has now settled at an average of seven percent year on year, but last year more than doubled in some regions.

Mortgage lending in the middle of the country grew by seven percent during the second quarter of 1997 compared with the same period last year, according to Barclays mortgage index which measures the activity of all mortgage lenders.
This region has now caught up with the south of England which also increased gross mortgage advances by seven percent over the period, said the homelender.
Barclays mortgage index is based on the flow of funds through solicitors' deposit accounts, of which Barclays has a market share of about 30 percent.
